title: Past Perfect: had + Past Participle
grammarTitle: Past Perfect — The Past Before the Past
grammarNote: Past Perfect (had + past participle) используется для описания действия, которое произошло РАНЬШЕ другого действия в прошлом. Это «более прошлое» прошедшее. Когда вы рассказываете историю в Past Simple и нужно вернуться назад к чему-то, что случилось ещё раньше — используется Past Perfect.

grammarTable.subject: I / You / He / She / We / They
grammarTable.example: "I had finished the report before she arrived." (finish = earlier; arrive = later)

grammarTable.subject: Negative
grammarTable.example: "He hadn't eaten breakfast when the exam started." (no breakfast before exam)

grammarTable.subject: Question
grammarTable.example: "Had she left before you arrived?" / "What had happened?"

grammarTable.subject: Key words
grammarTable.verb: before / after / when / already / by the time / just
grammarTable.example: "He had already left." / "By the time I arrived, she had gone." / "He had just finished."

grammarTable.subject: Purpose
grammarTable.example: Use PP to make clear which past event came FIRST when telling a story.

grammarTable.subject: Already
grammarTable.example: "By 2 p.m., she had already submitted the report." (before 2 p.m., she finished it)

grammarExtra.title: Past Perfect vs Past Simple — ordering events

rows.example: "When Amir arrived at the exam room, he sat down and started writing." (main events)
"He had prepared all evening." (this happened BEFORE he arrived — earlier past)
"When she entered, she smiled." (enter and smile = same moment → both Past Simple)
"When she entered, she had already heard the news." (heard = before entering)
"By the time she called, he had already left." — he left first, then she called.

rows.form: JUST: very recently in the past
rows.example: "When she arrived, he had just finished." — he finished moments before.

rows.form: NEVER / EVER: up to that past moment
rows.example: "He had never seen anything like it before that day." — up to that past moment.

rows.form: BY THE TIME: deadline in the past
rows.example: "By the time class started, she had reviewed all her notes." — before class.
"When I arrived, she had already gone." (gone = before my arrival)
"After he had finished the report, he went home." (finish = before going home)
"Rustam arrived at the professor's office." (main narrative time)
"He had been working on the project for weeks." (context: before he arrived)
"The assistant said she had tried to email him." (email = before the conversation)
"He arrived at the bus stop only to find the bus had already left." (left = before arrival)
✅ "Before she arrived, I had finished." — use PP for the earlier of two past events.
✅ Only use PP when sequence matters. "She woke up, got dressed, and left." → all Past Simple is fine.
✅ "He had GONE to the shop." — Past Perfect uses past PARTICIPLE, not past simple! ✅
✅ "She had already LEFT." — had + PAST PARTICIPLE. "left" not "leave"!

grammarTip:
Past Perfect = had + PAST PARTICIPLE

Используй когда нужно показать, что одно прошлое действие
произошло РАНЬШЕ другого прошлого действия:

"When I arrived, she had already left."
(she left → THEN I arrived — past perfect = earlier)

"He had prepared all week. The exam was easy."
(prepare happened BEFORE the exam)

Ключевые слова:
BY THE TIME + past simple → Past Perfect для ранней части
"By the time class started, I had reviewed everything."

ALREADY / JUST / NEVER + Past Perfect:
"I had already finished." / "She had just arrived."
"He had never seen it before."

⚠️ Ошибки:
✗ "He had went" → ✅ "He had gone" (3-я форма!)
✗ "She had already leave" → ✅ "She had already left"

exercises.instruction: Which action came first? Choose Past Perfect.
exercises.text: When Kamila arrived, Amir ___ already ___ the food.
exercises.hint: First: Amir ate. Then: Kamila arrived. Earlier event → Past Perfect. "HAD ALREADY EATEN." ✅

exercises.instruction: Put the verb in the correct tense.
exercises.text: "By the time the exam started, she ___ (review) all her notes."
exercises.hint: "By the time + past simple" → Past Perfect for the earlier action. "She HAD REVIEWED all her notes." ✅

exercises.text: "I had went to the library" is a correct Past Perfect sentence.
exercises.hint: ✅ "I had GONE to the library." — Past Perfect = had + past PARTICIPLE. "gone" ≠ "went." ✅
"The professor had left" — he left BEFORE the arrival. Earlier event → Past Perfect. ✅

exercises.text: "She didn't know the answer because she ___ (not study) the chapter."
exercises.hint: Reason = earlier action → Past Perfect negative. "She HADN'T STUDIED the chapter." ✅

exercises.text: "He had never visited Almaty before that trip."
opts: He visited Almaty before this, then again
"Never visited" = not once up to THAT past moment
exercises.correct: "Never visited" = not once up to THAT past moment
exercises.hint: "had never + pp" = no experience up to that point in the past. ✅ "He HAD NEVER VISITED Almaty before that trip."

exercises.instruction: Choose: Past Simple or Past Perfect?
exercises.text: "When I got to the bus stop, the bus ___ (already / leave)."
exercises.hint: Bus left BEFORE I arrived → Past Perfect. "The bus HAD ALREADY LEFT." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct past perfect form.
exercises.text: "She ___ (not eat) anything, so she felt dizzy."
exercises.hint: Earlier reason (not eating) → Past Perfect negative. "She HADN'T EATEN anything." ✅

exercises.instruction: When should you NOT use Past Perfect?
exercises.text: "She woke up, got dressed, and left." Should these be Past Perfect?
opts: Yes — always use PP for multiple past actions
No — they happen in sequence without a specific second reference point
Yes — "got" and "left" should be Past Perfect
exercises.correct: No — they happen in sequence without a specific second reference point
exercises.hint: Simple sequence in a story = Past Simple is fine! PP is only needed when you specifically want to show one action is BEFORE another reference point. ✅

exercises.text: "After she ___ (finish) the report, she sent it to her professor."
exercises.hint: "After" introduces the earlier action → Past Perfect. "After she HAD FINISHED, she sent it." ✅

exercises.text: "He realised he ___ (forget) his passport." (discovered earlier action)
exercises.hint: Discovery of earlier mistake → Past Perfect. "He realised he HAD FORGOTTEN his passport." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence with correct Past Perfect.
opts: "By the time he arrived, she had left."
"When he arrived, he had just see her."
exercises.correct: "By the time he arrived, she had left."
exercises.hint: "She HAD LEFT" = correct Past Perfect. ✅ Others: "ate" → "eaten"; "went" → "gone"; "see" → "seen."

questions.text: Past Perfect is used to show:
opts: Two actions happening at the same time
An action BEFORE another past action
questions.correct: An action BEFORE another past action
questions.hint: Past Perfect = the "earlier past." It happened before another past event. ✅

questions.text: "She had left." — Past Perfect is formed with:
questions.hint: had (for ALL subjects) + past participle. "She HAD LEFT." ✅

questions.text: "By the time class started, I ___ (review) all my notes."
questions.hint: "By the time + PS" → Past Perfect for earlier event. "I HAD REVIEWED all my notes." ✅

questions.text: "She had already ___ when I arrived." Choose.
questions.hint: Past Perfect = had + PAST PARTICIPLE. "gone" = past participle of "go." ✅ NOT "went" (past simple).

questions.text: "When I arrived, she had just ___ the meal." Choose.
questions.hint: "had just COOKED" — past participle of "cook." "When I arrived, she had just COOKED the meal." ✅

questions.text: "I had went there" — What is wrong?
questions.hint: ✅ "I had GONE there." — Past Perfect needs past PARTICIPLE (gone), not past simple (went)!

questions.text: "She hadn't eaten when I called." — "hadn't eaten" means:
opts: She was eating when I called
She had not eaten before I called
questions.correct: She had not eaten before I called
questions.hint: "hadn't eaten" = Past Perfect negative. She had not done this action before the call. ✅

questions.text: "Had you ever seen this before?" — This is:
questions.hint: "Had + subject + past participle?" = Past Perfect question. "HAD you ever SEEN this before?" ✅

questions.text: "He didn't study, so he ___ (fail) the exam before he knew it."
questions.hint: Earlier consequence → Past Perfect. "He HAD FAILED the exam before he knew it." ✅

questions.text: "She woke up, had coffee, and left." — Should Past Perfect be used?
opts: Yes — three events always use PP
No — simple narrative sequence uses Past Simple
questions.correct: No — simple narrative sequence uses Past Simple
questions.hint: Simple narrative sequence = Past Simple is fine. PP is for when you need to signal a SPECIFIC earlier action. ✅

questions.text: "He had never seen this before." — "before" means:
opts: Up to that specific moment in the past
questions.correct: Up to that specific moment in the past
questions.hint: "had never + pp + before" = not once, up to that specific past moment. ✅

questions.text: "After she ___ (leave), I cleaned the flat." (earlier action)
questions.hint: "After" + earlier action → Past Perfect. "After she HAD LEFT, I cleaned the flat." ✅
"He HAD ALREADY FALLEN asleep." = Past Perfect. "fallen" = past participle of "fall." The sleeping happened before the call. ✅
"By the time + [later event], [earlier event = Past Perfect]." "By the time she ARRIVED, he had left." ✅ "by the time" = the later reference.

questions.text: "The professor ___ (be call) to a meeting." (Past Perfect Passive)
questions.hint: Past Perfect Passive: "had been + past participle." "The professor HAD BEEN CALLED." ✅

questions.text: "She realised she had forgotten her keys." — "had forgotten" means:
opts: She forgot before she realised it
questions.correct: She forgot before she realised it
questions.hint: "had forgotten" = Past Perfect — the forgetting happened BEFORE the realising. Earlier past. ✅
